title: Nephron anatomy: filtration and tubular segments
description: Follow filtration through glomerular barrier, segmented tubules, medullary loop and collecting ducts.

questions.question: What are the main parts of a nephron?
questions.answer: A renal corpuscle filters plasma; proximal tubule, loop of Henle and distal tubule modify filtrate. Collecting ducts receive fluid from multiple nephrons.

questions.question: Where does filtration occur in the kidney?
questions.answer: Filtration occurs across the glomerular capillary barrier into Bowman space in the renal corpuscle, mainly in the kidney cortex.

questions.question: What is the bowman capsule?
questions.answer: Parietal squamous layer and visceral podocyte layer enclosing Bowman space. Function: Collects primary filtrate from glomerulus.

questions.question: Where are the podocyte foot processes located?
questions.answer: Interdigitating podocyte extensions with slit diaphragms over glomerular capillaries. Function: Final cellular component of filtration barrier.

questions.question: What is the function of the collecting duct?
questions.answer: Function: ADH-sensitive water reabsorption and acid/base regulation. Receives distal connecting tubules from multiple nephrons and descends through medulla.
